layout_note: Running-poetry layout: Proverbs set one aphorism per verse, each verse opening with a printed '†' divider and wrapping to at most a second indented line; a narrow LEFT-margin column carries a per-verse topical gloss (Mercie, Deuotion, Iuſt gaine, ...), while printed verse numbers 6-26 run down the RIGHT margin, with one scripture cross-reference beside v25.

body.text: † By mercie and truth iniquitie is redemed : and in the feare
of our Lord euil is auoided.
† When the wayes of man shal pleaſe our Lord , he wil
conuert alſo his enemies to peace.
† Better is a litle with iuſtice, then much fruite with iniquitie.
† The hart of man diſpoſeth his way : but it perteyneth to
our Lord to direct his progreſſe.
† :: Diuination is in the lippes of the king, his mouth shal not
erre in iudgement.
† Weight and balance are iudgements of our Lord : and his
worke al the ſtones of the bagge.
† They are abominable to the king that doe impiously :
becauſe the throne is eſtablisbed by iuſtice.
† The wil of kinges are iuſt lippes : He that ſpeaketh right
thinges shal be beloued.
† The kings indignation, meſſengers of death : and the wiſe
man wil pacifie it.
† In the cherfulnes of the kings countenance is life : and his
clemencie is as the later showre.
† Poſſeſſe wiſdom , becauſe it is better then gold : and gette
prudence,becauſe it is more precious then ſiluer.
† The path of the iuſt auoideth euils : the keper of his ſoule
kepeth his way.
† Pride goeth before deſtruction, and before ruine the ſpirit
shal be exalted.
† It is better to be humbled with the meeke, then to diuide
ſpoyles with the proude.
† The lerned in word shal finde good thinges : and he that
hopeth in our Lord, is bleſſed.
† He that is wiſe in hart,shal be called prudent : and he that is
ſweete in ſpeach shal finde greater thinges.
† A fountaine of life the lerning of him that poſſeſſeth it :
the doctrine of fooles foolishnes.
† The hart of the wiſe shal inſtruct his mouth : and shal adde
grace to his lippes.
† Wel ſet wordes are a honie combe:ſwetnes of the ſoule the
health of the bones.
† There is a way that ſeemeth to a man right : and the later
endes therof lead to death.
† The ſoule of him that laboureth doth labour to himſelf,
becauſe his mouth hath compelled him :
† The

marginalia.text:
:: God aſſiſteth
ſuperiors in
gouerning
their ſubiectes.
marginalia.note: opens with the '::' annotation-anchor mark that also stands in body line_index 7 before 'Diuination'

marginalia.text:
Iuſt balance do
pleaſe God &
good kinges.

marginalia.note: a small dash '-' is set at the left of the second line ('- reuerence of'); read as a stray/pointer mark, not included in gloss text; gloss spans vv.14-15 (no separate gloss printed for v15)
initial 'w' of 'Sweetnes' is in the small margin fount and could be a genuine 'vv'; rendered 'w' per roman prior, flagged

apparatus.note: marginal scripture cross-reference set beside v25; upper line reads 'ch.' plus a small raised mark, lower line reads '12.' or '11.'; digits not confidently legible at this raster resolution. Almost certainly points to the verbatim parallel at Proverbs 14:12 ('There is a way that seemeth right unto a man...').

anchor_marks_note: The paired '::' mark links body v10 ('† :: Diuination...') to its left-margin gloss (':: God aſſiſteth...'); it functions like the '‖' anchor in Genesis 24. Kept in the archaic text; downstream glyph_map may treat it as a strippable reference marker.

uncertain.note: printed with a closed-bowl letter after the round 's' that matches the 'b' in 'establi' on the same word, and differs from the open-leg 'h' in 'the'/'throne' on the same line — i.e. the plate appears to set 'eſtablisbed', a b-for-h printer's typo for 'established'. Preserved as printed per §typos; flagged because the b/h distinction is near the resolution limit. Intended word: established.
'sh' is a round-s + h (not ſh); the 'w' read as a real 'w' per the body w-regime (predominantly connected 'w' on this page); low residual ambiguity on w vs vv at the wre cluster.

initial 'w' in the small left-margin fount; could be genuine 'vv' (the fount where genuine vv survives) vs a real 'w'. Rendered 'w'; flagged. Note the body form at line 35 is spelt 'ſwetnes' (single-e, long-ſ) — a spelling/fount difference from this gloss.

right-margin cross-reference digits illegible at 400-DPI-class raster; content anchor (verbatim parallel Prov 14:12) suggests 'chap. 14, 12' but NOT copied into the text as fact — digits left flagged.

glyph_notes.long_s_policy: GLYPH-DRIVEN. Every 'sh' cluster on the page was zoom-checked: all seven 'shal' tokens (vv.7,10,13,18,20,21,23x2) are round-s + h → 'shal'; likewise 'showre' (v15), 'foolishnes' (v22), 'cherfulnes' (v15), 'fooles' (v22), 'impiously' (v12) are round-s. Long-ſ verified in pleaſe, alſo, diſpoſeth, progreſſe, ſtones, iuſtice, iuſt, ſpeaketh, meſſengers, wiſe, Poſſeſſe, wiſdom, becauſe, ſiluer, ſoule, deſtruction, ſpirit, ſpoyles, bleſſed, ſweete, ſpeach, poſſeſſeth, inſtruct, ſet, ſwetnes, ſeemeth, himſelf.
glyph_notes.w_regime: Body sets a real 'w' (When, wayes, wil, worke, Weight, wiſe, way, with, word, wordes, Wel, showre, ſweete, ſwetnes). Small left-margin glosses may carry genuine 'vv' in a few places (flagged on 'Sweetnes').
glyph_notes.count_note: not hand-counted; recompute by script from the text fields as the source of truth.

method: Visual-multimodal read of the newmode-jp2 raster (diag-reocr/newmode-jp2/proverbs-ch16.png) with per-region zoom crops (2.5x-4x) on every sh-cluster and ambiguous glyph; long-ſ vs round-s decided per glyph, not by position. Modern DR content used ONLY to confirm verse mapping (page runs Prov 16:6-26) and the likely referent of the v25 cross-reference, never as a spelling oracle.
confidence: high on body scripture glyphs (all sh-clusters zoom-verified); medium on the small left-margin topical glosses; flagged-low on 'eſtablisbed' (b/h), the 'Sweetnes' gloss w/vv, and the v25 marginal cross-reference digits.
